messages:
Alex: Quick follow-up from the Q&A — can someone clarify how credits interact with rate caps and burst behavior on the hosted API vs Dedicated? Example: a customer has $100 in credits, then 5x traffic spike. What gets enforced first (rate caps or credit exhaustion)? Also curious about short-term roadmap for per-route rate limits and visibility in the Console. Thanks.

Emma: Short answer: hosted usage is metered and credits offset billed usage until depleted. Rate-limits are independent of whether you have credits — credits don't change token rate limits. Dedicated is contract/reservation-based and is billed separately, so credits generally do not apply to Dedicated usage unless explicitly in the contract.

Sam: Technical note — we enforce throttling at the gateway with token and concurrency buckets (leaky-bucket style). Credits affect billing only, not the rate-limiter itself. If a customer exceeds their rate cap they get 429s regardless of credits. For Dedicated, traffic is isolated to the reserved pool so you won't hit org-global hosted rate caps, but you still have per-deployment concurrency and per-node safety limits.

Sam: Example headers we emit for hosted requests: 
```
X-RateLimit-Limit: 1500000
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 1498342
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1680000000
```
(we'll extend to per-route headers when we GA per-route caps)

Luis: To add — during capacity pressure we try graceful degradation first: routing to cheaper/compatible model variants, then fallbacks, and finally 429s with a Retry-After. We also surface a short "graceburst" so short spikes are absorbed where possible, but sustained 5x spikes will be throttled.

Mara: From Support perspective: please use the customer-facing doc we linked in the Q&A (https://redwood.example/docs/credits-and-quota) and if a customer expects a planned spike, have them open a priority ticket with: account id, expected peak qps/tokens, timeframe, and whether they are on Dedicated. We can then coordinate capacity or manual exceptions.

Emma: A couple of other billing points: promotional credits are consumed against hosted invoice items first. Credits typically expire after 6 months (exceptions handled case-by-case through finance). Refunds/credit stacking rules are in the billing FAQ.

Priya: Roadmap snippet: per-route and per-key caps + Console visibility are planned for next quarter (we're prioritizing per-key usage caps first). Goal: admins can set soft caps and hard caps by route, see live token burn, and apply webhook alerts. We'll sync product/finance/eng after this all-hands to align defaults.

Sam: Implementation note for visibility: backend will attach per-route metrics to existing token accounting and expose a Console tab + API. We'll GA with a canary rollout (feature flag) and allow orgs to opt in before enforced hard limits.

deploy-bot: feature-flag "per-route-caps" rolled out to staging at 2026-03-23T15:10:00Z (flag: staging/per-route-caps=true)

Alex: Awesome, that helps. Can we get a short one-pager for the support team summarizing what to tell customers re: credits vs rate caps?

Mara: Yep — will draft and drop in #support in the next hour.

Alex: Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
